correctness.rationale: A strict-contracting positive-probability edge word gives a unique compact invariant measure. Stationary update identities give internal edge disagreement decay -1/2 weighted squared difference; stubborn updates increase at most 5R^2, yielding 10 epsilon B R^2/lambda2. Conditioning on independent anchor selection gives the empirical-mean stationary recursion; comparison with a Wasserstein (1-1/(2N))-contracting affine chain yields the claimed errors. The Bernoulli-convolution variance and centered Gaussian sequential limit are computed from independent series weights. All normalization and boundary conditions are stated. The executable exact rational checker passes 290 first/second-moment and bound checks; it does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The source models explicitly distinguish weak versus strong stubborn influence but supply transient rather than complete weak-influence stationary law. A fixed-N asymptotic consensus can remain a nondegenerate random opinion even as the anchor frequency tends to zero, with topology erased at leading order and a spectral-gap-controlled finite-contact correction. This resolves a meaningful structural and order-of-limits question for all connected weighted networks rather than a tailored example, arbitrary parameter substitution, or known tabulation.
